title: Circular Reconfigurable Parallel Processor for Edge Computing : Industrial Product ✶
problem: GPUs suffer from sequential instruction execution and frequent data transfer overheads in their memory systems, leading to poor latency, area, and energy efficiency for edge computing applications. Traditional von-Neumann architecture is fundamentally suboptimal for edge computing deployment.
motivation: Edge computing applications require efficient hardware accelerators that can deliver high performance with minimal power consumption, which GPUs cannot provide cost-effectively.
method: RPP arranges computing engines in a circle that can be reconfigured for different tasks, with data flowing in a predictable stream instead of jumping around. It replaces complex routing systems with simpler linear switch networks and gasket memory (a specialized memory interface). To handle different types of data access efficiently, it layers the memory in a hierarchy and includes hardware features like concurrent kernel execution (running multiple programs simultaneously), optimized register splitting, and a mix of scalar (single-value) and vector (multi-value) processing. The system comes with a complete software stack—compiler, runtime, and code libraries—that lets programmers write code like they're using a GPU, even though the actual chip architecture is completely different.
key_novelty: It replaces traditional complex routing with a circular arrangement of compute engines using simple linear switches and specialized memory (gasket memory), while maintaining flexible data paths and memory reuse optimization.
contributions: Circular reconfigurable processor architecture optimized for edge computing
Circular network topology with gasket memory reducing routing overhead
Hierarchical memory system supporting flexible access patterns and mapping strategies
Complete software stack enabling GPGPU compatibility for broader adoption
